My eSorts as an Assemblywoman are rooted in amplifying marginalized and underrepresented voices. I am deeply committed to social justice, equality and opportunity for all. Please explain any activities and/or experiences that demonstrate your commitment to the LGBTQ movement. Please be specific. My approach to community building has consistently reflected my position as a firm ally of any and all LGBT individuals. As such, I wholeheartedly support progressive legislation that advances rather than reverses the fundamental right of LGBT individuals to be treated as equals under the scope of state law. As an Assemblywoman for 5 terms and have passed dozens of laws: --Extending the statute of limitations for unlawful discriminatory cases to 3 years --Prohibiting liquidated damages for plaintiSs in violation of their nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) in sexual harassment cases --Expanding the use of standby guardianship to include instances of immigration-related arrest, detention, and deportation --Requiring the Department of Health to collect and annually publish a list of policy-based exclusions from every New York hospital. Policy based exclusions are healthcare services a hospital is licensed for but does not provide. In partnership with Stonewall, I'd love to continue this work for many years to come! What are your policy priorities if you are to win this seat? How will these policy priorities impact the LGBTQ community? We have to pass the gender identity respect, dignity and safety act, let's get it done! The urgency of passing such legislation is amplified by its ability to protect the LGBT community from unacceptable discrimination and bigotry. Please list here the union, organizations (community, civic, media, issue groups), LGBTQ leaders, and elected o@icials that have endorsed you. We are still in the endorsement process for this election cycle. I have been endorsed by NYLCV and Queens County Dems. Previously, I have been endorsed by groups and organizations including but not limited to, AFL-CIO Citizen Action of New York, PPNYC, UFCW Local 1500, RWDSU, SEIU 1199, UFT, 2

How would you use your platform as a New York State Legislator to advocate for protection of LGBTQ people across the city, state and country? Overall, my goal would be to use my position as a New York State Assemblymember to be a tireless advocate for LGBTQ equality and justice, both within the state and beyond. By championing inclusive policies, fostering dialogue and understanding, coalition building, and mobilizing support from diverse stakeholders, I am committed to working towards a future where all LGBTQ individuals are treated with dignity, respect, and equality under the law. That's why I passed a law to ensure that every member of law enforcement in the state is trained in identifying hate crimes and understanding bias, as those often target members of the LGBTQ communities. By enacting meaningful reforms, providing oversight and accountability, and prioritizing the needs of marginalized communities, the legislature can help build a more just and inclusive society. New York State is experiencing a housing crisis and the LGBTQ community disproportionately experiences homelessness, especially our LGBTQ youth and seniors. How do we ensure that any plan is equitable to the LGBTQ Community and other marginalized groups? To ensure that any plan addressing the housing crisis in New York is equitable to the LGBTQ community and other marginalized groups, several key considerations should be taken into account: Policymakers should actively involve representatives from the LGBTQ community and other marginalized groups in the development of housing policies and programs. This includes consulting with LGBTQ advocacy organizations, community leaders, and individuals with lived experiences of housing instability and homelessness to ensure that their perspectives and needs are incorporated into the planning process. Housing initiatives should prioritize providing targeted support for vulnerable populations within the LGBTQ community, such as LGBTQ youth, seniors, transgender individuals, and people of color. ESorts to increase aSordable housing should prioritize LGBTQ-aSirming housing options that are safe, accessible, and aSirming of diverse gender identities and expressions. This could include expanding aSordable housing programs targeted towards low-income LGBTQ individuals and families, as well as investing in supportive housing models that oSer wraparound services tailored to the needs of LGBTQ community members, like culturally competent and responsive services, mental health support, case management, and peer support networks. With the repeal of Roe V. Wade and state legislatures across the country implementing abortion bans, New York State has become a safe haven for reproductive rights. In today’s political landscape, what do you see as the New York Legislature’s role in protecting and expanding reproductive healthcare? We have the responsibility to serve as a bulwark against attacks on reproductive rights and to champion policies that ensure access to comprehensive reproductive healthcare for all individuals in the state. The state should increase funding for family planning programs, expanding Medicaid coverage for reproductive healthcare services, and support initiatives to improve access in underserved communities. The legislature can support policies to ensure that all individuals have access to comprehensive, age- 4
